# Verified reference notes for the pilot

This section preserves the v1/v1.1 support record. The current additions and limits are in [Wave 1 evidence notes](wave-1-evidence-notes.md); use [retrieval status](retrieval-status.json) for the current cleared source inventory rather than treating the historical list below as exhaustive.

Ledger IDs cleared for the current corpus: **1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14**. IDs 6 and 8 were exploratory failed or unverified URLs and must not be cited. Metadata and mechanisms below were checked against retrieved PDF text or, for 9, the publisher abstract, rather than inferred from historical favicon-only citations. Retrieval used search and direct HTTPS download; the configured `web_extract` backend cannot extract pages. No ER performance claims are inferred from these retrievals.

| Ledger ID | Verified work | Specific support | Limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ivan P. Fellegi and Alan B. Sunter, *A Theory for Record Linkage*, JASA 64(328), 1183–1210, December 1969 | Sections 2–3: joint likelihood-ratio decision theory; conditional-independence simplification for additive weights; three dispositions; blocking discussed explicitly | Optimality for stipulated distributions/error constraints is not universal calibrated probabilities or optimal entity clustering. PDF is an IPUMS reprint with noisy OCR. |
| 2 | George Papadakis, Dimitrios Skoutas, Emmanouil Thanos, Themis Palpanas, *A Survey of Blocking and Filtering Techniques for Entity Resolution*, arXiv:1905.06167, retrieved August 2020 manuscript | Blocking, filtering, hybrid methods; classical and approximate candidate-generation families | Survey taxonomy and mechanisms, not universal performance guarantees; distinguish preprint and journal title/year. Do not copy the manuscript's placeholder DOI. |
| 3 | Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun, Kilian Q. Weinberger, *On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks*, ICML/PMLR 70, 1321–1330, 2017 | Calibration definition and post-processing; temperature scaling study | Empirical study is image/document classification, not ER. No claim that temperature scaling is best for linkage. |
| 4 | Olivier Binette, Youngsoo Baek, Siddharth Engineer, Christina Jones, Abel Dasylva, Jerome P. Reiter, *How to Evaluate Entity Resolution Systems: An Entity-Centric Framework with Application to Inventor Name Disambiguation*, arXiv:2404.05622v1 | Entity-centric labeling, estimators and diagnostics under defined sampling design | Inventor name disambiguation/simulations; not universal evaluation on incomplete labels. Retrieved PDF identifies v1, April 2024. |
| 5 | Olivier Binette and Rebecca C. Steorts, *(Almost) All of Entity Resolution*, arXiv:2008.04443 | Broad ER landscape, record linkage and clustering, statistical issues | Landscape context, not support for a particular proposed improvement. |
| 7 | Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jerome Friedman, *The Elements of Statistical Learning*, second edition, 2009, author-maintained download | Logistic regression, regularization, additive models and model assessment | General statistical foundations, not evidence logistic ER outperforms alternatives. See chapter 4.4 for logistic discrimination. |
| 9 | Indrajit Bhattacharya and Lise Getoor, *Collective Entity Resolution in Relational Data*, TKDD 1(1), 2007 | Publisher abstract supports joint resolution using relational co-occurrence | Full author-hosted PDF failed with 403; do not claim its full experiments were reviewed. |
| 10 | Indrajit Bhattacharya and Lise Getoor, *Online Collective Entity Resolution*, AAAI 2007 | Full primary paper supports adaptive query-time relational resolution | Publication databases and query-time study, not evidence that every incremental design outperforms batch. |
| 11 | Mauricio Sadinle, *Bayesian Estimation of Bipartite Matchings for Record Linkage*, arXiv:1601.06630v1, January 2016 | Sections 2, 3.4, 4–5: duplicate-free assumptions, competing links, assignment/likelihood conditions and unresolved outcomes | Comparison-vector independence and chosen loss assumptions are conditional; optimizing arbitrary pair sums is not automatically calibrated global inference. |
| 12 | Oktie Hassanzadeh, Fei Chiang, Hyun Chul Lee, Renée J. Miller, *Framework for Evaluating Clustering Algorithms in Duplicate Detection*, VLDB 2009 | Section 2.1: connected components/transitive closure, center-based alternatives; evaluation scope inspected | Primary algorithm description and context, not universal performance rankings. Sparse unscored pairs in Atlas remain unknown even where a published experimental graph completion convention differs. |
| 13 | Jens Bleiholder, Felix Naumann, *Data Fusion*, ACM Computing Surveys 41(1), Article 1, December 2008 | Sections 2–2.5: schema alignment → duplicate identification → fusion; value-preserving/conflict handling, preferred-source/mode/recency alternatives | Published article states 2008, not an assumed 2009 date. Source strategies do not prove field correctness, provenance independence or stable-ID correctness. |
| 14 | Serge Aleshin-Guendel, Mauricio Sadinle, *Multifile Partitioning for Record Linkage and Duplicate Detection*, arXiv:2110.03839v1, October 2021 | Sections 2–5: multifile partition, file-specific duplication and K-partite constraints, partial estimates with abstention | Bayesian source/duplication model is a distinct alternative, not evidence that generic greedy constraints improve every ER system. |

## Reasoning versus evidence
Candidate-set union monotonicity, expected-loss threshold derivations, odds transformations and metric definitions can be explained as mathematical reasoning with explicit assumptions. Proposed experiments and architecture contracts are Atlas synthesis, not attributed benchmark findings. Frequency and contextual-reliability hypotheses are untested adaptations of established evidence principles, not novelty claims.
